title: 09 Relating algebra and geometry: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 09 Relating algebra and geometry: Visual Guide

1. Same Two Differences | two draggable points on a grid with the right triangle, the midpoint dot, and live slope, distance and midpoint readouts | slope, distance and the midpoint are three different objects built from the same dx and dy, so distance subtracts and squares while the midpoint just averages the coordinates

2. Undoing Pythagoras | squares drawn on both legs and on the hypotenuse with their areas, next to four candidate answers computed live | the distance formula contains a square root because it inverts the Pythagorean theorem, which returns d squared, an area, when a length was asked for

3. Center And Radius | sliders for h, k, r and a test point, drawing the circle and the dashed distance line with an inside/on/outside verdict | the standard equation is the distance statement squared, so the center reads off with flipped signs and the constant on the right is r squared, not r

4. Complete The Square | the general form's D, E and F on sliders, run forward into standard form and backward into expanded form step by step | completing the square is the only way to recover the center and radius from an expanded equation, and the completed right-hand side decides between a circle, a single point and no real graph
